name: Upright bass
_what: A double bass, pizzicato. The `arco` articulations are a bowed
instrument and a different voice; `perc` is the body being hit and is
This library names its samples at the pitch they SOUND — `a0` is 28 Hz
— so unlike Black And Blue there is no octave correction. The tool
measures every note it writes either way.
The key and the velocity live on the `<group>` here and only `sample=`
is on the region, which is why render_voice parses SFZ headers properly
_notes: This is the one bank whose grid is the LIBRARY'S and not this tool's.
Meatbass samples every third semitone — A0, C1, Eb1, Gb1 and up — so
the five-semitone spacing the electric basses use is not available: the
choice is every 3 (ten notes in range, 11.3 MB, past what this voice is
F#1, A1 and C2 at the library's own three-semitone spacing, then every
six up to F#3. That keeps the whole bottom octave, where a bass line
actually walks, within a semitone of a sample, and spends the worst
stretch of three on Eb2, A2 and Eb3 higher up. Three semitones is the
engine's limit rather than a comfortable number, and this is the voice
_release: Not the source's literal number. Meatbass declares `ampeg_release=0.001`
with `ampeg_sustain=0`, which is a library saying 'the sample IS the
decay, there is no release stage' — the decay is on CC102 and the
player lets the note ring. One millisecond in our engine is not that,
it is a step to zero on every note, which is a click on every note. So
this bank takes the contract's default of 60 ms, which is a hand landing
on a string, and the sample carries the ring as the library intended.
